title: First 'Nature Listening Festival' Held in Finland
paragraphs: Imagine an outdoor festival where you can listen to several different acts, but instead of musicians you are listening to birds singing, the wind in the trees, and the gentle sound of flowing water.

That's the idea of Hilja Fest, the world's first nature-listening festival which is now being held in Finland. Hilja means "quietly" in Finnish, and it has been called the "world's quietest festival."

Hilja Fest is taking place in Valkmusa National Park, which is about a 90-minute drive to the east of Helsinki. This is an area of swampland with 40 different wetland habitats. It has forest paths and wooden boardwalks, resting stops and observation towers, which make it easy for visitors to explore and enjoy.

The stars of the festival are insects, birds, plants, animals, the morning mist and rocky cliffs! But unlike a music festival, where you might find yourself rushing from one stage to another, at Hilja Fest visitors are encouraged to take their time, listening, watching and enjoying each of these natural stars in their own habitat.

Simo Peri, the creative director of Hilja Fest said, "We have planned the first ever Festival of Nature Listening so that visitors get to tour the national park and really listen to the music nature creates."

The festival organizers list 13 natural stars on four "stages" that can be found around the park. These include birds like black grouse and common cranes, animals like the common lizard, and plants like cranberries, cloudberries and sundews. But there is no schedule, and some performers — like a very rare moth, called the "purple bordered-gold" — might not turn up at all!
Visitors are simply encouraged to "Stop. See how much is happening when everything else goes quiet."
The festival began on October 10 with an invitation-only event, but is now free for anyone to enter and will continue until October 31.
